projects.summary: MultiQ runs independent quantum circuits together on neutral atom processors.
projects.overview: MultiQ compiles circuits into virtual zone layouts. Its controller bundles layouts and schedules shared hardware operations. A checker verifies circuit independence.
method: Virtual zone layouts separate compilation from physical placement.
The controller schedules independent circuits across the same processor.
The checker verifies that shared execution preserves each circuit.
projects.result: The evaluation reports throughput gains from 3.8 to 12.3 times for 4 to 14 concurrent circuits.
notes: The publication list assigns CGO 2027. The linked preprint appeared in January 2026.

projects.summary: Chipmunq maps fault-tolerant circuits onto modular quantum chiplets.
projects.overview: Chipmunq partitions circuits while preserving logical qubit patches. Its mapping and routing account for chiplet connections and defective qubits.
method: Partitioning preserves logical qubit patches.
Mapping accounts for sparse connections between chiplets.
Routing incorporates defective qubits and hardware constraints.
projects.result: The evaluation reports 13.5 times faster compilation than the compared tools.
notes: The source lists the same paper under Arxiv 2026 and XXX 2027.
XXX is an unresolved venue placeholder. The website should use the verified preprint status.

projects.summary: MCMit combines hardware control and software mitigation for measurements during quantum circuit execution.
projects.overview: MCMit reduces errors from measurement and classical feedback. It combines a branch instruction, qubit-state classifiers, and compiler transformations.
method: A multi-control branch instruction reduces classical feedback latency.
Neural classifiers identify qubit states from short readout traces.
Compiler transformations mitigate remaining branching errors.
projects.result: The Qubic evaluation reports up to 70 percent lower feedback latency.

projects.summary: A multi-stage Mamba model classifies superconducting qubit states from readout signals.
projects.overview: The first stage classifies qubit states. A refinement stage identifies errors caused by qubit relaxation. The model supports short measurement windows.
method: A Mamba model processes readout sequences.
The first stage classifies the initial qubit state.
The refinement stage reduces relaxation errors.
projects.result: The lightweight model reaches 0.906 geometric mean readout fidelity with 49.6 percent fewer parameters than the compared method.
notes: Mamba Readout is a website navigation label, not an official project acronym.
The publication list contains no resource links. The arXiv record confirms the title, authors, and QCE acceptance.

projects.summary: qTPU combines quantum processors and classical accelerators through hybrid tensor networks.
projects.overview: Hybrid tensor networks represent quantum and classical computation together. qTPU provides a programming model, compiler, and runtime for this representation.
method: The programming model expresses hybrid computation through tensor networks.
The compiler balances classical computation cost against quantum error.
The runtime executes across quantum processors and classical accelerators.
projects.result: The evaluation reports over 20 times faster execution across hybrid machine learning, circuit knitting, and error mitigation workloads.
notes: The lab lists Christian B. Mendl. The USENIX record lists Christian Mendl.

projects.summary: Zero-G decodes the sparse error signals left by a quantum pre-decoder.
projects.overview: A pre-decoder resolves simple local errors before the main decoder runs. Zero-G uses the remaining sparse signals to reduce decoding latency.
method: A pre-decoder resolves simple local errors.
Zero-G uses approximate matching to decode the residual signals.
A shared decoding core supports CPU and FPGA execution.
projects.result: The evaluation reports 10 times lower latency than existing strong decoders at matching accuracy.

Experiments compare classifiers and measurement durations.
The framework measures the resulting logical error rates.
projects.result: The study finds that shorter measurements can preserve logical error rates within the evaluated hardware conditions.

projects.overview: Harvest compiles lattice-surgery programs under a shared resource model. It coordinates circuit placement, routing, and magic-state generation. It then removes unused layout space.
method: The resource model supports multiple magic-state generation protocols.
Placement and routing account for circuit demand and congestion.
A final pass reclaims unused layout patches.
projects.result: The benchmark evaluation reports an average speedup of 4.83 times over sequential execution.

projects.summary: QVM uses gate virtualization to run large quantum circuits on smaller processors.
projects.overview: Gate virtualization replaces selected two-qubit gates with separate operations and classical reconstruction. QVM compiles and executes the resulting circuit fragments.
method: A virtual circuit representation records virtual gates.
Compiler passes optimize the circuit fragments.
The runtime executes fragments and reconstructs the original result.
projects.result: The IBM evaluation runs circuits with up to twice the processor qubit count.
notes: The earlier arXiv version has the title Scaling Quantum Computations via Gate Virtualization.
